client_visible_changes: 0.23.0 adds no route and preserves the 44 routes of 0.22.0 (ADR 0010). The exec and session start schemas now publish the optional read_only_roots list the wire crate has always admitted: closed {host_path, mount} entries, each path absolute and canonical, at most MAX_READ_ONLY_ROOTS (4) entries, no mount equal to, beneath or above one substrate owns or another root's. A start that names none serializes and hashes exactly as before.

The capability facts object (schemas/capability.json) and the observed resource union (schemas/resource.json) are closed, and 0.23.0 adds the optional exec.read-only-roots fact, the closed {max_roots: 4}, to the one and, to every applied confinement shape, an optional read_only_roots member listing each bound root as declared. A client that validates snapshots or resources against predecessor 0.22.0 rejects a snapshot that publishes the fact, or a record of a start that bound a root, until it moves to 0.23.0.

A correction of emitted members: the exec applied confinement now admits read_only_files and secret_slots in every state, and in the expired and unknown states also read_only_roots, workdir, writable_roots and an aperture network, as the wire crate's AppliedConfinement emits them. Bundles 0.5.0 to 0.22.0 rejected the record of an exec that placed a secret slot, and 0.18.0 to 0.22.0 the record of one that bound a read-only file; their bytes are frozen and keep that defect.

No refusal is new. The three a declared root has always raised are now published, each a 422 refused before the program starts: exec.read-only-root-invalid for a broken lexical rule, and exec.read-only-root-absent and exec.read-only-root-not-a-directory for a host path that is not present or not a directory reached without a symlink. The daemon answers a start in this order: the capability snapshot and the start's other confinement members first (egress apertures, secret slots, read-only files, writable roots and the working directory, each its rule and then its capability), then the root list's lexical rule, then the roots capability, so a start naming a root on a host that does not publish exec.read-only-roots is refused exec.sandbox-unavailable (501) before dispatch and no root is ever run unmounted. The two host refusals come last, from the driver.

The session start now publishes the three exec fields exec start already did (design 27): its exec object gains the optional scratch, measurements and workspace_access members, each the same schema as on exec start. A session start has always decoded them, and the daemon and driver have always admitted and applied them exactly as on exec start, with the same refusals, after the session's own gates. A client that validates session starts against predecessor 0.22.0 rejects a session naming one of them; a session start naming none serializes and hashes exactly as before.

The refusals those three members have always raised are now published, on exec start and session start alike (design 27, amendment 2), as an x-b10x-refusals annotation on each member: measurements raises exec.metrics-unserved (501); scratch raises exec.scratch-quota-unserved (501) and exec.scratch-quota-limit (507); workspace_access raises exec.workspace-access-invalid, exec.workspace-subtree-absent, exec.workspace-subtree-symlink, exec.workspace-subtree-not-directory and exec.workspace-subtree-changed (422) and exec.workspace-scoped-write-unserved (501). No refusal is new.

The daemon now refuses, as request.schema-invalid (422), three values every published start schema already refused (design 27, amendment 3): scratch null, a storage max_bytes that is not a multiple of 1024, and a measurement listed twice. A client that validated against the schema sees no change; one that sent these values relied on the daemon reading null as absent, rounding nothing and collapsing the duplicate. The 1024-byte unit also applies to a workspace's storage, which shares the storage-limit definition, so a misaligned workspace quota is refused at admission instead of storage.quota-limit from the host.
development_constraints: This development bundle is contract-execution-ready but cannot satisfy a stable dependency.
Passing the bundle gate proves bundle integrity; it does not claim producer or host-driver conformance.
No compatibility promise begins before a signed stable release.
